_comment: Cell-identity allowlist for the LTE analogue of Signal #5 (S1 Setup
Request), same pattern as detector/allowlist.json (5G NG Setup) and
detector/allowlist_gsm.json (2G LAI/ARFCN).
Every legitimate eNodeB in this lab must appear here with the EXACT
(PLMN, eNB ID, TAC) tuple it presents in its S1 Setup Request's
Global eNB ID and Supported TAs IEs. Any S1 Setup Request whose tuple
is not listed here is flagged as a cell-identity allowlist violation
(candidate rogue eNodeB).
Values below come straight from config/srsran/enb.conf (enb_id) and
config/srsran/rr.conf (tac) - this lab's one legitimate eNodeB - NOT
hardcoded into the detector script, so the same detector works
unmodified against a different lab or a different set of legitimate
eNBs: just edit this file.
How to read an eNB's own identity off a real S1 Setup Request using
tshark:
- plmn.mcc / plmn.mnc: from the S1 Setup Request's Global eNB ID,
tshark fields e212.mcc / e212.mnc.
- enb_id: from tshark field s1ap.macroENB_ID (a hex byte string,
20 significant bits of a macro eNB ID per TS 36.413 9.2.1.37),
interpreted as an unsigned integer of the raw byte string. For
this lab's enb.conf, enb_id = 0x19B produces macroENB-ID
0x0019b0 on the wire (0x19B left-shifted 4 bits to fill the
20-bit field with 4 pad bits, per the macro eNB ID encoding) -
the detector compares the raw on-wire value, not the config
file's own enb_id, since that's what's actually observable.
- tac: from the Supported TAs List's TAC field, tshark field
s1ap.tAC, reported in decimal.
